title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page): S is a base with 2 invertible, and E/S is an elliptic curve. J = E[2] − {0} is the étale cubic cover formed by the three nonzero 2-torsion points. Σ_J is the twisted P^1 (a conic) obtained as E/{±1}, with the divisor D_J ≅ J of branch points. Σ*_J = Σ_J − D_J. A Legendre pinning (épinglage de Legendre) is equivalent to a triple (J, t, α):
- a) J is the étale cubic cover;
- b) t ∈ Σ*_J(S) is the fourth branch point, the image of the origin; it plays the role of λ in y² = x(x−1)(x−λ);
- c) α is an isomorphism between a fixed μ-type rank-one object H^×_4 and ω_J. Here ω_J is the orientation (discriminant) double cover of J, i.e. the two cyclic orderings of the three points.

This page computes the automorphisms of such an object, to show that the fibred category (stack) is not rigid. Automorphisms are induced by automorphisms of J, i.e. sections of the finite étale group scheme G_J = Aut_S(J), a twisted form of S_3. Each automorphism of J extends uniquely to Σ_J, since a projective transformation is determined by three points.

Compatibility with c) forces the automorphism to preserve orientations, so it lies in G^+_J, the twisted A_3. As an S-scheme, G^+_J ≅ S ⊔ ω_J: the unit section together with the two 3-cycles. The two 3-cycles are in canonical bijection with the two cyclic orientations, which is why they form ω_J.

An automorphism that is non-identity on every geometric fibre is therefore a section ρ of ω_J. Such a ρ exists only if ω_J is trivial, and it makes J a torsor under (Z/3Z)_S, since ρ cyclically permutes J.

Compatibility with b) means ρ(t) = t. So t is a section of the fixed-point subscheme P_J = (Σ*_J)^{G^+_J} ⊂ Σ*_J. On the standard model J = {0,1,∞}, ρ is λ ↦ 1/(1−λ), and its fixed points are the roots of λ² − λ + 1 = 0, i.e. λ = −ω, −ω² (primitive sixth roots of unity). These are the equianharmonic curves with j = 0, the 'courbes exceptionnelles' of the next page.

Purpose: to explain why the Legendre stack has nontrivial automorphisms, exactly over j = 0. Grothendieck then rigidifies on the next page by adding a trivialization J ≅ {0,1,∞}_S (Legendre–Jacobi pinning of level 2). The rigidified stack is then U_{0,1} × G_m, i.e. the λ-line times a unit.
errors: The machine transcription reads the torsor group as (Z/2Z)_S. A 3-cycle makes J a torsor under (Z/3Z)_S, and the image appears to read Z/3Z.

Implicit gap: in characteristic 3, which the cote's 'char ≠ 2' does not exclude, ρ: λ ↦ 1/(1−λ) has the single double fixed point λ = −1 (since λ² − λ + 1 = (λ+1)²). So P_J is a non-reduced length-2 subscheme, not an étale double cover, and j = 0 = 1728 is supersingular. The scheme-theoretic definition of P_J as the fixed locus handles this, but the étale picture breaks down.
The page treats only automorphisms coming from Aut(J). Whether the automorphism −1 of E acts trivially on the data, via α, is not discussed on this page.

ideas.what: Automorphisms of a Legendre-pinned elliptic curve are the sections of the even part G^+_J ≅ S ⊔ ω_J of the twisted S_3 = Aut(J) that fix t; nontrivial ones exist exactly over the j = 0 locus P_J
ideas.modern_name: Automorphism groups / inertia of the Legendre (Γ(2)-type) moduli stack; S_3 action on the λ-line with fixed points at sixth roots of unity
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Legendre, Klein, the anharmonic group); stack-theoretic form in Deligne–Rapoport (1973) and later level-structure literature

ideas.what: Decomposition of the twisted alternating group scheme G^+_J of an étale cubic cover as unit section ⊔ discriminant (orientation) double cover ω_J
ideas.modern_name: Discriminant / sign double cover of an étale cubic algebra; twisted form of A_3
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (theory of étale cubic algebras, resolvents; e.g. Knus et al., Book of Involutions)

ideas.what: Encoding the Legendre λ as a point t of the twisted conic Σ*_J attached to J, so that the λ-line becomes a form of P^1 − 3 points over the stack of cubic covers
ideas.modern_name: Twisted Legendre family; M_{1,1}[1/2] described via forms of P^1 minus three points

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but classical computation: the stabilizers of the S_3 action on the λ-line occur at j = 0. It is done in a twisted, stacky language. The formulation is elegant, but nothing here would be new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: 'contours' should be 'automorphismes': 'un objet peut avoir des automorphismes non triviaux ... Les automorphismes définis par des automorphismes de J'.
First line: 'Le champ en question n'est pas rigide' (with the crossed-out 'Le défaut des').
'schémas en groupes étales G_J' likely refers to the group scheme Aut_S(J); the marginal note under S reads 'correspond à la section unité du schéma en groupes'.
The last line likely expresses P_J as the fixed-point subscheme of G^+_J acting on Σ_J, roughly 'P_J = (Σ_J)^{G^+_J}' (circled).
